clue.text: Road surface touched a river from behind

indicators.note: reading from behind means the run of pieces is taken back to front

parts.note: touched in the sense of slightly crazy
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A motorist backs into a river and the road surface is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' applies to the whole run of three pieces, not just the river; the Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac's ancestor: a road surface of compacted broken stone named after the engineer McAdam.

clue.text: Wrong application is filed by brood

indicators.note: filed by means placed in among, so the word is enclosed

parts.note: to brood is to muse, ponder

explanation.surface: A misapplied document has been filed by a gloomy clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filed by' reads like office work, but it means slotted in among the letters of the brooding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or wrong use of something, so a wrong application of it.

clue.text: In the pink, Beethoven's Fifth his ultimate symphony?

indicators.note: In means the letter goes inside the colour

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour

indicators.note: Fifth picks the fifth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Beethoven's Fifth in fine shape, and his final symphony mentioned too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fifth here is a letter, not the famous symphony: H; 'In' puts it inside CORAL. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ninth, his last completed symphony, is nicknamed after its sung finale with chorus.

clue.text: Unconscious chap in parent, wally

indicators.note: in means placed within the parent word

parts.note: dad is a parent
under means anaesthetised, unconscious
he refers to a male, a chap

explanation.surface: A knocked-out man inside a father: a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wally' is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a stupid person, a blockhead.

clue.text: Preserved body, something to keep well!

parts.note: one keeps mum, staying silent
well! and my! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: An embalmed corpse is something one would keep in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something to keep' points to the phrase 'keep mum', stay quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmed corpse, as from ancient Egypt, is a body preserved.

clue.text: False claim about electoral fraud starts to get nasty

indicators.note: a false claim is a made-up one, so these letters are reconstructed
the starts of the two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A bogus allegation of vote-rigging is about to turn the campaign ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAIM plus E and F, from 'starts to' electoral fraud, rearranged by 'False'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for harmful or malevolent, the opposite of beneficent.

clue.text: Hand on lid on brown cocktail

parts.note: a hand is a worker, a man
lid is slang for a hat
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A hand placed on a brown lid, then a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiskey and vermouth cocktail named after the New York borough.

clue.text: Places I pass going north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A traveller heads north through a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns I + COL round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of locus, a place or position, used in maths and genetics.

clue.text: Jungle tribe having no time for this delicate matter?

indicators.note: having no means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a jungle is a tropical forest
kin is family, one's tribe

explanation.surface: An anthropologist reports on a jungle tribe too busy for a delicate subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes T from FOREST. The definition is a coy nod to circumcision, a delicate matter in more than one sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition: this sensitive fold of skin is literally delicate tissue.

clue.text: Patron wants snooker player to pocket most balls

indicators.note: to pocket means to take inside

parts.note: a cuer is someone using a cue

indicators.note: balls means nonsense, so the word most is scrambled

explanation.surface: A patron wants a snooker player to sink most of the balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' rearranges MOST into STOM; 'to pocket' puts it in CUER.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or business is a client who buys from it.

clue.text: See 20
Horny stars in movies, or economists looking back?

indicators.note: looking back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about sexy film stars or randy economists, peering back over their shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters within 'movies, or economists'; 'looking back' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Unicorn, a creature with a single horn, so its stars are horny.

clue.text: A mouse of a pussy?

parts.note: a cat as timid as a mouse is a fearful feline, playground slang for a coward

explanation.surface: Asks about a cat that behaves like the mouse it ought to chase.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mouse' is a timid person; a cat who is one is a cowardly cat, the childish insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a timid cat, and the childish name for any coward.

clue.text: Freezing temperature thus encapsulating capital, ultimately, in European city

parts.note: zero degrees Celsius, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing the next letter

parts.note: thus means so

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word capital

explanation.surface: A weather report on a frozen European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulating' puts L, 'ultimately' from capital, inside SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway, a city in northern Europe.

clue.text: One looking up name inspired by art, or some fake

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the letter is taken inside
fake means forged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An art expert looks up a name in some forged works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' looks like a forgery in the art story but signals a rearrangement; 'inspired by' means breathed in, taking the letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying the stars and planets spends their time gazing skywards.

clue.text: Greek character with enemies to take on in Tuscany

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
antis are those against something
to take on staff is to hire them

explanation.surface: A Greek and his foes hiring help in Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a jokey British nickname for Tuscany, after its Chianti wine and the many English middle-class holiday homes there.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous British nickname for the Italian region, coined from its Chianti wine country plus a shire.

clue.text: I'm in a state, a state of exuberance

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next phrase

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone flustered declares they are in a state, though an excited one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm in a state' sounds like distress, but 'in' is a container signal, and the first 'a state' is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness and spirited energy, a condition of high spirits.

clue.text: Box containing one key, a long key

indicators.note: containing means holding the next pieces inside

parts.note: to box in training is to spar
an ace is a one in cards
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A box holding a single key and a long one, like a locksmith's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' first means a musical key, then a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: The widest key on a computer keyboard, a long bar along the bottom.

clue.text: Reptile, one going on foot?

definitions.meaning: a venomous American pit viper snake
a soft leather shoe, which goes on the foot

explanation.surface: A snake slithering along beside a walker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the water snake of the southern US and a soft Native American shoe bear this name.

clue.text: Reformed Tory a pain around nick, describing testing on release

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the next piece
reformed means made over in new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: nick means steal, rob

explanation.surface: A reformed Conservative in pain near a police station, on the theme of offenders tested after release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' sounds like a mended criminal but signals an anagram; 'around' wraps it round the word for nick, which here means steal, not prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a trial period of supervision after release, so this adjective describes such testing.

clue.text: Almost certainly a cold month, August normally feels less unsettled initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A sniffle in a cold month, though August usually feels steadier.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition teases that a man's dramatic illness is almost certainly a common cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking term for a cold exaggerated by a man into grave illness.

clue.text: Gorilla biting bottom of Britney Spears going ape in cafe

indicators.note: biting means holding the next letters between its jaws

parts.note: a gorilla is slang for a thug, a goon

indicators.note: going ape means going wild, so the letters are jumbled
the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A gorilla bites a pop star's backside in a cafe, gone berserk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going ape' shuffles the singer's surname with her last letter ('bottom of'); 'biting' then sets that block inside the thug just after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for a cheap, basic cafe serving fried food.

clue.text: Mistake not getting up for early bird?

indicators.note: not getting means the word up is left out

parts.note: a cock-up is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Sleeping in is the mistake of someone who should have risen early.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK-UP is British slang for a mess or blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooster crows at dawn, so it is literally an early bird.

clue.text: Fern — girl getting shock

parts.note: a maiden is a young girl
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A girl gets a fright on discovering a fern.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate fern of the genus Adiantum, with fine fan-shaped fronds.

clue.text: Material processed underground that's brought to the surface

indicators.note: brought to the surface means moved upwards, read backwards in a down entry

parts.note: mined means dug and extracted underground

explanation.surface: Something dug up in a mine is a material.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Symbol to write down on top of orders

parts.note: to log something is to record it

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clerk notes a symbol at the head of an order form.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem or mark that identifies a company or brand.

clue.text: European's taken to US citizen

indicators.note: European has taken to inside, so the word is enclosed

parts.note: a Bosnian is a European, from Bosnia; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A European has warmed to an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to' looks like 'grown fond of', but the 's is 'has': the European has taken the word to inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of Boston, Massachusetts, so a citizen of a US city.

clue.text: A car endlessly following leader of monstrous criminal organisation

indicators.note: following means the pieces come after that first letter
the leader of a word is its first letter
endlessly means losing the final letter

parts.note: Fiat is an Italian car make

explanation.surface: A car chase involving a monstrous crime boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' docks the Italian car's last letter; 'following' puts the A and the car after the first letter of monstrous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian crime syndicate, the archetypal organised-crime network.

clue.text: Escape cheese in Cheshire town

parts.note: escape means run away
cheese in the sense of something trite or sentimental, corny stuff

explanation.surface: A prisoner flees with some cheese in Cheshire, a county famous for its cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county in the north-west, famed for its crumbly cheese; Runcorn is an industrial town there.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Mersey estuary in the county of Cheshire, north-west England.

clue.text: Happy to describe copper as metal

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw a line round, enclosing

parts.note: happy means merry
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to call copper a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something; copper is a chemical symbol here.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver, the liquid element, is a metal.
